svg.text: Validator scoring & expert routing
How MR1's semantic agreement determines the domain-aware committee selected in MR2
MR1 — global-score committee selection
S₁(v) = G(v)
First-mini-round score is simply the validator's global reliability score.
W(v) = ⌊α · S₁(v)⌋
Selection weight scales with score. The first validator drawn becomes leader;
the rest form the committee. A weight that floors to zero is not eligible.
MR1 certificate
A subdomain is retained only if supported by at least
Q = ⌊2G/3⌋ + 1 of the G committee votes — producing a
quorum-backed subdomain-frequency map, freq(d) for d ∈ D.
G = committee size · Q = quorum · α = scaling factor
freq(d)
MR2 — domain-weighted committee selection
w_d = freq(d) / Σ_(d′∈D) freq(d′)
Each subdomain's weight is its share of the selected batch's label frequency.
S₂(v) = Σ_(d∈D) w_d · DScore(v, d)
Validators specialized in the subdomains actually present in this batch
score higher for this round than generalists.
Same weighted-selection mechanism
W(v) = ⌊α · S₂(v)⌋ reuses MR1's deterministic weighted-draw
procedure, evaluated with the domain-aware score instead of
the global score — so expert routing follows semantic evidence,
not a leader's unilateral choice.
DScore(v,d) = validator v's domain-specific score for subdomain d
Adversarial selection risk (equal-weight baseline)
Probability that a committee of size c, drawn from N validators containing M malicious ones, selects a malicious semantic quorum.
Over R independent rounds the cumulative probability is 1 − (1 − P(X ≥ q))ᴿ: small committees carry non-negligible cumulative risk,
while larger committees reduce it significantly. This is not just a block-validation concern — the selected group also contributes the
signed semantic evidence (labels in MR1, classifications in MR2) that routes and judges the next mini-round.
